proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
D^0_{a,u}(x)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=a,S=1,X=x]
-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=a,S=0,X=x].
\]
We first prove necessity of (1).  Fix \(u\), a finite \(g\le u\), and \(c\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Since \(c>u\), global mean no anticipation at both \(u-1\) and \(u\), consistency, and subtraction give
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X]=m_{c,1,u}(X).
\tag{5}
\]
The no-ineligible-effect condition and consistency similarly give
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X]=m_{c,0,u}(X).
\tag{6}
\]
Hence \(D^0_{c,u}(X)=d_{c,u}(X)\).  The global OVS parallel-gap condition applied once with comparison \(c\) and once with comparison \(c'\) yields
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=D^0_{g,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X),
\]
which proves (1).  Notice that the argument uses \(c>u\), not the stronger and generally inappropriate requirement \(c>t\).

For sufficiency, suppose (1) holds.  The never-adopting cohort belongs to every \(\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), so define the common observable gap
\[
\delta_u(x)=d_{\infty,u}(x).
\tag{7}
\]
Equation (1) implies \(d_{c,u}(x)=\delta_u(x)\) for every \(c>u\) whenever a post-adoption restriction is indexed at \(u\).  Enlarge the observed probability space only by independent auxiliary variables.  On units with \(S=0\), set \(Y_v(a,0)=Y_v\) for every \(a\) and \(v\); this gives consistency and no ineligible effect.  On an eligible unit with finite factual cohort \(a\), set its factual path \(Y_v(a,1)=Y_v\), set \(Y_v(\infty,1)=Y_v\) for \(v<a\), and, recursively for \(v\ge a\), choose
\[
\Delta Y_v(\infty,1)=m_{a,0,v}(X)+\delta_v(X)+\xi_{a,v},
\qquad E_Q[\xi_{a,v}\mid G=a,S=1,X]=0.
\tag{8}
\]
One may take \(\xi_{a,v}=0\); independent centered bounded variables may instead be used without changing any displayed mean.  For \(G=\infty,S=1\), take the observed path as the never-treated path.  Set all remaining counterfactual coordinates equal to the corresponding never-treated path.  This specifies a joint law on the declared finite potential-outcome array and preserves the observed marginal.

The pre-\(a\) equality of the two paths in (8) proves mean no anticipation.  Moreover, for every finite \(g\le u\), (8) and the ineligible construction give
\[
D^0_{g,u}(X)=m_{g,0,u}(X)+\delta_u(X)-m_{g,0,u}(X)=\delta_u(X).
\tag{9}
\]
For every \(c>u\), equations (5)--(7), which hold for the constructed paths because they coincide with the observed paths before \(c\), give \(D^0_{c,u}(X)=\delta_u(X)\).  Equation (9) is therefore exactly every global OVS conditional-parallel-gap restriction.  Thus the construction belongs to \(\mathcal M\), proving the full-data-to-observed equivalence.

We next prove tangent exhaustion.  For a retained cell and period put
\[
U_{a,s,u}(O)=\frac{\mathbf 1_{a,s}}{p_{a,s}(X)}
\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,s,u}(X)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Global retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition imply \(U_{a,s,u}\in L_2(P)\), and the definition of \(m\) gives \(E_P[U_{a,s,u}\mid X]=0\).  Along any regular dominated observed submodel with score \(s\), the quotient rule for a conditional mean gives
\[
\dot m_{a,s_0,u}(x)
=E_P[U_{a,s_0,u}(O)s(O)\mid X=x].
\tag{11}
\]
Indeed, differentiating the conditional numerator and denominator and subtracting \(m_{a,s_0,u}(x)\) yields (11).  Therefore the derivative of the left side of (1) is
\[
\dot d_{c,u}(x)-\dot d_{c',u}(x)
=E_P[Z_{u;c,c',P}(O)s(O)\mid X=x].
\tag{12}
\]

Let \(D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) be the finite vector of conditional linear maps in (12), restricted to the deterministic independent formal rows \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Necessity implies
\(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  The reverse inclusion follows from the conditional-mean interior condition, as we now verify rather than assume.  Start with a bounded \(s\in\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and the dominated tilt \(dP_\epsilon^0=(1+\epsilon s)dP\) for sufficiently small \(|\epsilon|\).  The exact conditional-mean quotient and (12) show that every violation of (1) under \(P_\epsilon^0\) is \(O(\epsilon^2)\).  Conditional on each \((G,S,X)\), the vector of increments is finite dimensional.  Because its mean is in the relative interior of its conditional convex support, every sufficiently small mean displacement in the linear span of its centered support is produced by a bounded likelihood tilt of that conditional law.  Apply such tilts, cell by cell, to cancel the finite vector of \(O(\epsilon^2)\) violations.  On sets where the available relative-interior radius is at least \(j^{-1}\), the correcting likelihood ratio is \(1+O(j\epsilon^2)\); these sets increase to probability one.  First let \(\epsilon\to0\), and then \(j\to\infty\).  The resulting exact-model submodels have scores converging to \(s\) in \(L_2(P)\).  Directions orthogonal to a conditional centered-support span require no correction, because their conditional means cannot change under any dominated tilt.  Truncation followed by the same finite conditional correction shows that bounded kernel elements are dense in \(\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}=\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\tag{13}
\]

For completeness, this construction has not inserted a hidden full-data restriction: every corrected observed law still satisfies (1), so the extension in (7)--(9) lifts it to a full-data law in \(\mathcal M\).  Conversely every induced observed submodel satisfies (1) by necessity.

Let \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) denote the right side of (2).  If \(s\in L_2^0(P)\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), then, for every coordinate \(e\) and every bounded measurable scalar \(a(X)\),
\[
0=E_P[a(X)Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}s]
=E_P[a(X)E_P[Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}s\mid X]].
\]
Testing successively with bounded truncations of the sign of the conditional expectation shows \(E_P[Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}s\mid X]=0\) almost surely.  Hence \(s\in\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Conversely, that conditional equality makes \(s\) orthogonal to every square-integrable measurable multiple of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and therefore to its closure.  Thus
\[
\mathcal N_{\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp=\ker D_{\mathrm{OVS}}=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}.
\]
Taking orthogonal complements of closed subspaces proves (2).

The identical argument applied to the explicitly declared local rows in Definition \(\ref{def:local-observed-model}\) proves (3).  If a local row uses \(k=(g,t)\), \(k'=(g,t')\), \(u\le\min(t,t')\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\), then \(c>t\ge u\) and \(c'>t'\ge u\).  Thus \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), so every local row is a global OVS row.  This proves the second inclusion in (4) and, by orthogonal complementation, the tangent inclusion.

For two comparisons in one target block, direct subtraction of Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
R_{k,c,P}-R_{k,c',P}
=-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{u=g}^t Z_{u;c,c',P}.
\tag{14}
\]
Every summand in (14) is a local row, so measurable aggregate clean-comparison contrasts lie in \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\).  Closure proves \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\), completing (4).

Finally, take \(T=4\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{4,\infty\}\), and degenerate \(X\), with positive cell probabilities.  Choose bounded conditional means satisfying
\[
d_{4,2}=1,\qquad d_{4,3}=-1,
\qquad d_{\infty,2}=d_{\infty,3}=0.
\]
Then the cumulative contrasts agree because \(1-1=0\), but the period-two equality fails.  Necessity rules out both a local and a published OVS extension.  This proves the final assertion.

The tangent-normal identity in the first display is equation (2) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\).  The reference-score-gradient lemma gives, for every \(s\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\),
\[
\dot\tau_{\omega,P}[s]=E_P[\psi_P^0s].
\tag{23}
\]
We calculate the orthogonal projection of \(\psi_P^0\) onto the normal space without assuming invertibility.  Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), \(K(x)\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.  If \(v\in\ker K(x)\), then
\[
0=v'K(x)v=E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X=x],
\]
so \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and
\[
v'r(x)=E_P[v'Z\psi_P^0\mid X=x]=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
r(x)\in\{\ker K(x)\}^\perp=\operatorname{range}K(x),
\qquad K(x)K(x)^\dagger r(x)=r(x).
\tag{24}
\]
The Moore--Penrose map is Borel measurable because, for a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix,
\[
K^\dagger=\lim_{j\to\infty}(K^2+j^{-1}I)^{-1}K.
\tag{25}
\]

Put \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r'K^\dagger Z\).  Symmetry, (24), and the Moore--Penrose identities give
\[
E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
=r'K^\dagger KK^\dagger r
=r'K^\dagger r
=E_P[\psi_P^0p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\mid X].
\tag{26}
\]
Consequently \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\in L_2(P)\).  For every measurable \(a\) for which \(a(X)'Z\in L_2(P)\),
\[
E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})a(X)'Z]
=E_P[a(X)'\{r(X)-K(X)K(X)^\dagger r(X)\}]=0.
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (26)--(27) and tangent exhaustion prove
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\psi_P^0.
\tag{28}
\]
Combining (23) and (28) shows that \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) represents the derivative and belongs to the tangent space; it is therefore the canonical gradient.  Taking expectations in (26) proves (16).  If two Moore--Penrose coefficient versions differ in \(\ker K(X)\), their products with \(Z\) agree almost surely, so singularity does not make the projected random variable ambiguous.

Apply the same calculation to the local normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\psi_P^0.
\tag{29}
\]
Because \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), nested orthogonal projections imply
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}
\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\cap\mathcal T_P,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}).
\tag{30}
\]
The terms on the right of (30) are orthogonal.  Pythagoras proves (17).  Also \(p_{\mathrm{per},P}\) belongs to the published normal space, so subtracting it from the ambient gradient preserves (23) on the published tangent: this proves validity of the local gradient in the subclass.  It is canonical there exactly when it belongs to \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\), which, by equation (2) of the observable-equivalence theorem, is equivalent to (18).

We now establish the aggregate identities.  On the observable equality model, Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and the zero conditional means of all residual terms give
\[
E_P[\Psi_P\mid X]=Ah(X).
\tag{31}
\]
Thus every feasible loading has conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\), and iterated variance gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\tag{32}
\]
By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), \(A'b^\star=\omega\) and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  For \(d=b-b^\star\), feasibility gives \(A'd=0\), hence \(d=Nz\) for a measurable \(z\).  It follows that
\[
d'\Gamma b^\star=z'N'\Gamma b^\star=0.
\]
Expanding (32) proves (19)--(20), including uniqueness only modulo \(\ker\Gamma(X)\cap\ker A'\).

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) place weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other coordinates.  Then \(A'b^{\mathrm{ref}}=\omega\) and \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Since \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star\in\operatorname{col}N\), equation (14) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) yields
\[
p_{\mathrm{agg},P}:=\psi_P^0-\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star(X))'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{33}
\]
Moreover, (31), \(N'A=0\), and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\) imply
\[
E_P[N'R_P\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]
=N'\{\Gamma_P+Ahh'A'\}b^\star=0.
\tag{34}
\]
Therefore \(p_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\psi_P^0\).

The nested normal spaces are
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Successive projection increments are orthogonal, so
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}+(p_{\mathrm{per},P}-p_{\mathrm{agg},P})
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P})
+(p_{\mathrm{per},P}-p_{\mathrm{agg},P}).
\]
Pythagoras proves (21).  Finally, orthogonality to every measurable multiple of a finite normal vector is equivalent, by conditional expectation, to its conditional cross-moment with that vector being zero.  Applying this first to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and then to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) proves the two equality characterizations, including (22).

Let \(\eta=(p,m)\),
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X),
\qquad
\mu_P(O)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O).
\]
Conditional on a training complement, the validation observations are independent of its foldwise estimates by fixed-fold cross-fitting.  For \(k=(g,t)\), write \(M_{a,s,k}=\sum_{u=g}^tm_{a,s,u}\) and let \(B_{k,c}\) denote the bracketed numerator in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Adding and subtracting each true regression and taking conditional expectations gives the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}-B_{k,c}\mid X]
={}&\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{g,0}}{\widehat p_{g,0}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{g,0,k}-M_{g,0,k})\\
&+\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,1}}{\widehat p_{c,1}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,1,k}-M_{c,1,k})\\
&+\left(p_{g,1}-\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,0}}{\widehat p_{c,0}}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,0,k}-M_{c,0,k}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{43}
\]
Global overlap makes every coefficient Lipschitz in \(\widehat p-p\).  The fixed number of cells and periods and H\"older's inequality therefore imply
\[
|P\{\mu(O;\widehat\eta)-\mu(O;\eta)\}|
\le C\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,4}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{44}
\]

The OVS orthogonal-signal lemma and the global observable equalities give
\[
\|E_P[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\eta)=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O).
\tag{45}
\]
The OVS finite-support rate proposition gives
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2+a})=o_P(1).
\tag{46}
\]
The conditional fourth-moment envelope, nuisance consistency, and (46) imply
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X)'\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\tag{47}
\]
Equations (45)--(46) also show that the conditional mean of the difference in (47) is \(O_P(n^{-1})\): the signal drift is a propensity--regression product, while the learned-coefficient error multiplies that drift.  Conditional Chebyshev inequality applied fold by fold to (44) and (47), followed by summation over the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\{\mu_P-alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\}
+o_P(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{48}
\]
apart from the target-share ratio contribution.

The final estimator uses the global empirical target share \(\widehat\pi_{g,1}=\mathbb P_n\mathbf 1_{g,1}\).  Global overlap gives \(\pi_{g,1}\ge\varepsilon\), and Taylor expansion of the reciprocal gives
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})+O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{49}
\]
The mean bracketed numerator of each reference score in target block \(k=(g,t)\) is \(\pi_{g,1}\theta_k(P)\).  Hence (49) contributes
\[
-\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}
(\mathbb P_n-P)\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{50}
\]
By Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), combining (48) and (50) replaces \(\mu_P-E_P\mu_P\) exactly by \(\psi_P^0\).  Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\) then gives
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\{\psi_P^0(O_i)-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X_i)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i)\}+o_P(1)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{51}
\]

The summands in (51) are independent and identically distributed, mean zero, have finite second moment by overlap and the fourth-moment envelope, and have variance \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) proves the Gaussian limit in (41).  The estimated influence values contain the target-share correction in (50) and the OVS-complete orthogonal signal.  Equations (46)--(47), root-\(n\) consistency of the finite cell ratios and shares, and conditional Chebyshev imply
\[
\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2=o_P(1).
\]
Expanding the centered sample second moment therefore proves \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Division by its positive probability limit and the definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) prove (42).  The complete-normal canonical-gradient theorem identifies the variance in (41) as the published-class bound, proving attainment.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For one signed cell term, conditional expectation gives
\[
E_P\left[\widetilde m_{a,s,u}(X)
+\frac{\mathbf 1_{a,s}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}(X)}
\{\Delta Y_u-\widetilde m_{a,s,u}(X)\}\,\middle|\,X\right]
=\widetilde m_{a,s,u}
+\frac{p_{a,s}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(m_{a,s,u}-\widetilde m_{a,s,u}).
\]
Subtracting \(m_{a,s,u}\) turns the right side into
\[
\frac{\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}
(\widetilde m_{a,s,u}-m_{a,s,u}).
\]
Summing with the four declared signs proves (35).  Every summand is a product of a propensity error and a regression error, so the derivative in either nuisance direction vanishes when the other nuisance is fixed at its truth.  The observable equivalence theorem gives \(g_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}=d_{c,u}-d_{c',u}=0\), while substitution of \(\widetilde\eta=\eta\) into the definition gives \(S_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_{e,P}^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Finally, clipping bounds every reciprocal by \(2/\varepsilon\).  The triangle inequality followed by H\"older's inequality bounds each coordinate in \(L_2(P_X)\) by \((2/\varepsilon)\|\widetilde p-p\|_4\|\widetilde m-m\|_4\).  Summing the fixed finite number of signed coordinates and rows proves (36).

There are finitely many values of \(X\), cells, periods, and OVS rows.  Global overlap and the lower bound on each support mass imply that every training subsample contributing to a cell average has order \(n\) observations with probability tending to one.  For a scalar cell variable \(W\) with finite second moment, conditional variance and Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
\widehat E_{-\ell}[W\mid G=a,S=s,X=x]
-E_P[W\mid G=a,S=s,X=x]=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{39}
\]
The global conditional fourth-moment envelope applies (39) to increments and to every product needed for a second moment.  Because all index sets are fixed and support masses are bounded below, taking maxima and the \(L_4(P_X)\) norm preserves the order.  Thus \(\widehat p-p\), \(\widehat m-m\), and the preliminary target ratios are all \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).

The orthogonal-signal lemma and clipping show that replacing \((p,m)\) by their cell averages changes each signal in \(L_4(P)\) by \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), while its conditional mean changes only by \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  Expanding
\(\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}}\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}-Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}Z^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}\) and applying H\"older's inequality proves the first term in (37).  The same expansion of \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}}\widehat\psi^0-Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi^0\) proves the second.  Shared cohort--period cells create off-diagonal terms in these products, but the cell average estimates those cross-products directly; no block-diagonal approximation is used.

Fix a support point \(x\).  Since the law and support are fixed, the finite set of positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)\) has a positive minimum, if it is nonempty.  The variational characterization of ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
|\lambda_j(\widehat K(x))-\lambda_j(K(x))|
\le\|\widehat K(x)-K(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{40}
\]
Because \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\) and \(\tau_n\to0\), (40) separates every zero eigenvalue from every fixed positive eigenvalue.  A union bound over the finite support and folds proves simultaneous rank recovery.

On the recovered range, the inverse identity
\[
\widehat K_R^{-1}-K_R^{-1}
=\widehat K_R^{-1}(K_R-\widehat K_R)K_R^{-1}
\]
and the fixed-law positive eigenvalue minimum give an \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) inverse error.  Combining this with (37) proves the sharper rate following (38).  Without conditioning on recovery, every retained inverse eigenvalue is at most \(\tau_n^{-1}\), so (37) and the triangle inequality give the conservative rate (38).  Substitution of \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) yields \(n^{-1/2+a}\); its square is \(n^{-1+2a}=o(n^{-1/2})\) exactly when \(a<1/4\), and multiplication by \(n^{-1/2}\) is also \(o(n^{-1/2})\).  This proves all claims.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}=\{c\in\mathcal G:c>u\}\), where \(\infty>u\), and let \(d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x)\).  Under the global OVS no-anticipation and DDD conditional-parallel-gap conditions in Definition \(\ref{def:target-model}\), an observed law \(P\) admits a full-data extension \(Q\in\mathcal M\) if and only if
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\) for which some finite \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfies \(g\le u\), and every \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Thus the published class uses every cohort clean at period \(u\), including a cohort with \(u<c\le t\) that is unavailable as a single clean-through-\(t\) comparison for a terminal target \((g,t)\).

At a conditional-mean interior law, the published observed tangent orthocomplement is
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{2}
\]
The larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of Definition \(\ref{def:local-observed-model}\), which retains only cohorts clean through a target's terminal period, instead has
\[
\mathcal T_P^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Every local formal row is an OVS row.  Consequently
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp,
\qquad
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P.
\tag{4}
\]
The cumulative equalities \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\) are necessary in both models but, whenever a target spans more than one period, do not in general imply even the localized period-specific equalities.

Let \(P\) be a conditional-mean interior observed law induced by a full-data law in the global OVS model \(\mathcal M\).  Under global retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition,
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\]
With the objects in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\),
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}
\tag{15}
\]
is the canonical gradient of \(\tau_\omega\) in the published class, including singular and redundant fixed-law cases, and
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)].
\tag{16}
\]
The former complete-normal gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) is the canonical gradient only in the larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  It remains a valid gradient in the published subclass, but
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\tag{17}
\]
with equality if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{18}
\]

The conditional loading \(b^\star\) remains the singular-safe optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family.  In particular,
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b^\star(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)],
\tag{19}
\]
and every measurable feasible \(b\), with \(A'b(X)=\omega\) almost surely and \(b(X)'\Psi_P\in L_2(P)\), satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b(X)-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b(X)-b^\star(X))]\ge0.
\tag{20}
\]
The three nested frontiers obey
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{can},P})^2]
+E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2].
\tag{21}
\]
Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) reaches the localized bound exactly when
\(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0\), and it reaches the published OVS bound exactly when
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{22}
\]

\left\{\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}

\qquad

proposed.name: Localized period-specific normal projection
proposed.construction:
Let \(\mathscr E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) contain every nonzero triple \(e=(u,c,c')\) for which there exist \(k=(g,t)\), \(k'=(g,t')\in\mathcal K\) with the same \(g\), \(u\in\{g,\ldots,\min(t,t')\}\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\).  Associate the formal cell-incidence row
\[
\rho_e=e_{(c,1,u)}-e_{(c,0,u)}-e_{(c',1,u)}+e_{(c',0,u)}.
\]
The deterministic set \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{per}}\) is the lexicographically first maximal linearly independent subcollection of these rows.  Define \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) from these coordinates by the residual formula already displayed in this definition, and set
\[
\psi_P^0=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\Psi_{k,c_0(k),P},\quad
K_P(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}Z_P^{\mathrm{per}\prime}\mid X],\quad
r_P(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\psi_P^0\mid X],
\]
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=r_P(X)'K_P(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{per}},\quad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{per},P},\quad
V_{\mathrm{can}}=E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}^2].
\]
These are the projection and bound for the localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  The definitions of \(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\), \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\), and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}\) are unchanged.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old construction and metadata must identify its rows as localized after the global OVS basis is added.

proposed.name: Published OVS complete normal projection
proposed.construction:
For every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\) for which some finite \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfies \(g\le u\), let \(\mathscr E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) contain all nonzero rows indexed by \(e=(u,c,c')\) with distinct \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\):
\[
\rho_e=e_{(c,1,u)}-e_{(c,0,u)}-e_{(c',1,u)}+e_{(c',0,u)}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) be the lexicographically first maximal linearly independent subcollection of these formal rows.  For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), set
\[
Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}_{e,P}(O)=
\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,1,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,0,u}(X)\}
-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',1,u}(X)\}
+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',0,u}(X)\},
\]
and stack these coordinates as \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  With \(\psi_P^0\) from Definition \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\), define
\[
K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}\mid X],\qquad
r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi_P^0\mid X],
\]
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}},\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P},\qquad
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}=E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2].
\]
Use zero-dimensional conventions when there is no nonzero OVS row, and set \(\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This construction names every period-admissible published normal and its singular-safe projection.

proposed.name: Orthogonal published OVS normal signal
proposed.construction:
For \(e=(u,c,c')\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), set
\[
g_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(x)=d_{c,u}(x)-d_{c',u}(x).
\]
For a candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) with positive retained propensity coordinates, define \(Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\) by replacing \((p,m)\) with \((\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\), and put
\[
S_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)
=\widetilde d_{c,u}(X)-\widetilde d_{c',u}(X)
+Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta),
\qquad
\widetilde d_{a,u}=\widetilde m_{a,1,u}-\widetilde m_{a,0,u}.
\]
Stack the coordinates in \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{OVS}}\)-order as \(S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\), with the zero-dimensional convention.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The learned exhaustive correction must include the restriction level to remove first-order regression-centering drift.

proposed.name: Published OVS-complete efficient cross-fitted estimator
proposed.construction:
For each training complement of \(I_\ell\), estimate all globally OVS-retained propensities and one-step regressions by \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\), clipped to the overlap interval, and form
\[
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}=S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i;\widehat\eta^{-\ell}),
\qquad \widehat\eta^{-\ell}=(\widehat p^{-\ell},\widehat m^{-\ell}).
\]
Using training-cell averages, form
\[
\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell\prime}\mid X=x],
\qquad
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}\mid X=x],
\]
where \(\widehat\psi^{0,-\ell}\) uses the denominator-corrected reference scores and training-sample preliminary ratios.  Retain eigenvalues of \(\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)\) exceeding \(\tau_n\), use the Moore--Penrose inverse of the retained part, and set
\[
\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x)
=\{\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS},\tau}^{-\ell}(x)\}^{\dagger}
\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(x).
\]
For each target block, form the cross-fitted bracket numerator \(\widehat B_{i,k,c_0(k)}^{-\ell}\), but divide its final sample average by the global empirical share
\(\widehat\pi_{g,1}=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\).  Equivalently, write the resulting raw ratio pseudo-outcome as \(\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}\).  Return
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac1n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}
\left\{\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\right\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat\theta_k=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}\).  For \(i\in I_\ell\), define
\[
\widehat\phi_i=
\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k
\left\{\widehat R_{i,k,c_0(k)}
-\widehat\theta_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\widehat\pi_{g,1}}\right\}
-\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X_i)'
\widehat S_i^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell},
\]
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
(\widehat\phi_i-\overline{\widehat\phi})^2,
\qquad
\overline{\widehat\phi}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\phi_i,
\]
and report \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Both the construction and its metadata must move from the local normal to the exhaustive OVS normal.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}=\{c\in\mathcal G:c>u\}\), where \(\infty>u\), and let \(d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x)\).  Under the global OVS no-anticipation and DDD conditional-parallel-gap conditions in Definition \(\ref{def:target-model}\), an observed law \(P\) admits a full-data extension \(Q\in\mathcal M\) if and only if
\[
d_{c,u}(X)=d_{c',u}(X)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}
\tag{1}
\]
for every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\) for which some finite \(g\in\mathcal G\) satisfies \(g\le u\), and every \(c,c'\in\mathcal C_u^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Thus the published class uses every cohort clean at period \(u\), including a cohort with \(u<c\le t\) that is unavailable as a single clean-through-\(t\) comparison for a terminal target \((g,t)\).

At a conditional-mean interior law, the published observed tangent orthocomplement is
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{2}
\]
The larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of Definition \(\ref{def:local-observed-model}\), which retains only cohorts clean through a target's terminal period, instead has
\[
\mathcal T_P^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Every local formal row is an OVS row.  Consequently
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp,
\qquad
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P.
\tag{4}
\]
The cumulative equalities \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\) are necessary in both models but, whenever a target spans more than one period, do not in general imply even the localized period-specific equalities.
proposed.justification: This theorem identifies the exact observed image and exhausts the tangent normals of both the literal published OVS class and the larger clean-through-terminal local model.
proposed.gap: The published DDD-CPT indexing contributes period-admissible normal rows that are absent from target-terminal pairwise comparisons; prior staggered-DiD tangent results do not prove this DDD full-data extension.
proposed.consumer: The theorem determines which projection is the published-class canonical gradient and which restrictions software must include.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Dependencies, free symbols, and notes must follow the narrowed global/local theorem.

proposed.statement:
Let \(P\) be a conditional-mean interior observed law induced by a full-data law in the global OVS model \(\mathcal M\).  Under global retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition,
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\]
With the objects in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\),
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}
\tag{15}
\]
is the canonical gradient of \(\tau_\omega\) in the published class, including singular and redundant fixed-law cases, and
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)].
\tag{16}
\]
The former complete-normal gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) is the canonical gradient only in the larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  It remains a valid gradient in the published subclass, but
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\tag{17}
\]
with equality if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{18}
\]

The conditional loading \(b^\star\) remains the singular-safe optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family.  In particular,
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b^\star(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)],
\tag{19}
\]
and every measurable feasible \(b\), with \(A'b(X)=\omega\) almost surely and \(b(X)'\Psi_P\in L_2(P)\), satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b(X)-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b(X)-b^\star(X))]\ge0.
\tag{20}
\]
The three nested frontiers obey
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{can},P})^2]
+E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2].
\tag{21}
\]
Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) reaches the localized bound exactly when
\(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0\), and it reaches the published OVS bound exactly when
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{22}
\]
In particular, score-family projection is not called semiparametric efficiency unless (22) is verified.
proposed.justification: The theorem delivers the published OVS information bound, proves its singular-safe exhaustive projection, and nests the former local and aggregate frontiers beneath it.
proposed.gap: Constant or covariate-conditional pairwise-score optimization omits published period-admissible restriction normals unless its full conditional projection equation is verified.
proposed.consumer: The result supplies the efficiency benchmark and distinct aggregate, local-model, and published-class diagnostics.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem metadata must name the new OVS normal objects and preserve the local projection only as a larger-model benchmark.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(P\) is a fixed conditional-mean interior law induced by the global OVS model, \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, and every first stage in Definition \(\ref{def:crossfit-estimator}\) is its corresponding training-cell average.  Under independent fixed-\(T\) sampling, global retained-cell overlap, the global conditional fourth-moment envelope, fixed-fold cross-fitting, the threshold condition, and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\), take \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) for \(0<a<1/4\).  Then
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V_{\mathrm{OVS}}),
\tag{41}
\]
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\longrightarrow_P V_{\mathrm{OVS}},
\qquad
P\{\tau_\omega(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the OVS-complete-normal estimator attains the pointwise semiparametric efficiency bound of the published class.  The local complete-normal correction remains regular on the published subclass but need not attain its smaller bound.  No continuous-covariate, rank-uniform, or equality-boundary inference claim is made.
proposed.justification: The exhaustive orthogonal OVS correction turns the published population bound into an attainable pointwise procedure on fixed finite covariate support.
proposed.gap: The proof uses training-cell averages and is neither continuous-covariate nor rank-uniform.
proposed.consumer: An optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend can expose this branch for fixed discrete covariates.

prose_updates.tldr: The target is a fixed aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the literal global Ortiz--Villavicencio--Sant'Anna conditions.  At each post period \(u\), the published class uses every cohort \(c>u\), generating an OVS normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) that can strictly contain the old clean-through-terminal normal.  Exhausting that tangent normal gives \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}}\), where \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\) is now explicitly the larger localized-model bound.  Conditional loading \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) remains only the aggregate score-family optimum unless it satisfies the full OVS projection equation.  A cross-fitted exhaustive-normal estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) with pointwise Wald inference for fixed finite-support covariates.  In that same regime the comparator gap is a finite-dimensional smooth fixed-rank functional and supports pointwise inference away from equality; continuous-covariate and equality-boundary gap inference remain open.  The bounded binary witness retains its exact \(3/512\) full-bound gain because its single local normal already spans the OVS normal.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna impose DDD-CPT globally over every treated cohort, post period, and cohort clean at that period, but their estimator combines terminally clean pairwise scores with constant componentwise weights and does not derive the published observed tangent space or efficiency bound.  Existing staggered-DiD efficiency theory does not supply the coupled eligibility-gap full-data extension, denominator correction, or shared-cell DDD normal system.
project_justification.niche: The global published class contains period-admissible restrictions that disappear if controls are required to remain clean through a selected terminal target.  This creates three distinct precision frontiers: conditional pairwise-score loading, the larger localized equality model, and the smaller published OVS model.
project_justification.fill: The note proves full-data-to-observed equivalence for the literal OVS indexing, constructs deterministic local and OVS incidence bases, exhausts both tangent normals, and derives their singular Moore--Penrose projections.  It proves \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}}\le V_{\mathrm{agg}}\), supplies exact equality diagnostics, and attains the published bound with an orthogonal cross-fitted correction on fixed finite support.  It also supports fixed-law delta-method inference for positive comparator gaps in that regime and preserves the bounded \(3/512\) regression-test witness.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the global OVS DDD-CPT condition: for every finite treated cohort \(g\), every post period \(u\ge g\), and every period-admissible comparison cohort \(c>u\), the covariate-conditional untreated eligibility gaps agree.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell in the retained OVS support has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\); this includes cells used only by period-admissible normal rows and not by a terminal pairwise score.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For proved attainment, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below.  Fixed-fold training-cell averages estimate all OVS-retained propensities and one-step regressions, the augmented signals \(S_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}=g_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}+Z_e^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\).  Eigenvalues are thresholded with \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  In the same fixed-support regime, the comparator gap is evaluated as a finite-dimensional function of cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments, with the same deterministic rank threshold applied to every Moore--Penrose and KKT system.

prose_updates.related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna supply the causal assumptions, pairwise doubly robust scores, and constant componentwise GMM benchmark.  Their DDD-CPT assumption is global in period-admissible controls, whereas the earlier draft analyzed only a clean-through-terminal localization.  The present result exhausts the additional published normal rows and proves the corresponding smaller bound.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie provide related conditional-efficiency geometry for staggered DiD, but not the DDD full-data extension, eligibility-gap incidence system, or shared target-share derivatives.  Newey motivates generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; here range inclusion, nested projections, rank recovery, and the fixed-support remainder are derived for the DDD objects.  Generic DML results motivate cross-fitting, while the orthogonal OVS signal and all shared-cell products are established directly.  The bounded binary construction remains a full-bound comparison because its unique nonzero clean-comparison row spans both the localized and OVS tangent normals.
prose_updates.interpretation: A cohort can be a valid OVS control at an early period \(u\) even if it adopts before a target's terminal period \(t\).  Those early-period cells cannot enter a single cumulative terminally clean pairwise score, but they do create valid restriction normals and can lower the information bound.  Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) solves the aggregate conditional GLS problem, \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) solves the larger clean-through-terminal model, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) solves the literal published model.  A comparator is fully efficient only when its conditional cross-moment with \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) vanishes.  The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend should expose the exhaustive-normal method only for supported discrete-covariate designs, report aggregate and full diagnostics separately, and retain the user's prespecified \(\omega\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law.  Moore--Penrose projection permits singular and redundant normal coordinates because only the fitted normal random variable is identified.  Statistical attainment and positive efficiency-gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support, fixed-law rank recovery, separated positive fixed-law spectra, fourth moments, and nondegenerate limiting variances; neither result is uniform over rank changes.  Gap inference is restricted to \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\ge\delta_0>0\), because the first derivative can degenerate on the equality boundary.  A growing-sieve Riesz representation remains a population/general-covariate device and does not establish continuous-covariate Wald inference.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal class is the global OVS class, not the larger target-localized analogue.  The note separately reports the localized bound to quantify the information added by cohorts that are clean only at earlier periods.  The published canonical gradient and bound are population pointwise results.  Their cross-fitted attainment, variance consistency, and Wald coverage hold for fixed finite-support covariates with support masses bounded below, training-cell averages, and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  Positive comparator-gap inference uses the same finite-dimensional fixed-support regime, locally stable ranks, positive gap and influence variance, and thresholded Moore--Penrose systems.  Continuous-covariate attainment, continuous-covariate gap Wald inference, equality-boundary tests, and rank-uniform inference are not claimed.  The \(3/512\) witness remains a published full-bound result only because its one-normal closure equality is proved.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\), abbreviate \(t=t_{J_n,P}\), \(G=G_{J_n,P}=E_P[tt^{\prime}]\), \(g=g_{\Delta,J_n,P}\), and \(D=D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:complete-normal-tangent-projection}\), applied to each coordinate of the declared dictionary, gives
\[
t_j=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\{v_j-E_P[v_j]\}\in\mathcal T_P,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,J_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathcal T_P\) is a linear subspace,
\[
\mathcal S_{J_n,P}=\{c^{\prime}t:c\in\mathbb R^{J_n}\}\subseteq\mathcal T_P.
\tag{2}
\]

The range condition required by the Moore--Penrose formula is a consequence, rather than an additional assumption.  If \(c\in\ker G\), positive semidefiniteness and the definition of \(G\) imply
\[
0=c^{\prime}Gc=E_P[(c^{\prime}t)^2].
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(c^{\prime}t=0\) in \(L_2(P)\).  Since \(D\) is, by the premise of the theorem, a well-defined linear functional on \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\), Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) yields
\[
c^{\prime}g=\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}c_jD[t_j]=D[c^{\prime}t]=D[0]=0.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently \(g\in(\ker G)^{\perp}\).  Since \(G\) is a finite-dimensional symmetric matrix,
\[
(\ker G)^{\perp}=\operatorname{range}(G),
\qquad GG^{\dagger}g=g.
\tag{5}
\]

Put \(a=G^{\dagger}g\) and \(\zeta=t^{\prime}a\).  By Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), this is \(\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}\), and (2) gives \(\zeta\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\subseteq\mathcal T_P\).  For any \(s=c^{\prime}t\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\), symmetry of \(G^{\dagger}\), (5), and linearity of \(D\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\zeta s]
&=a^{\prime}Gc
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}Gc
=g^{\prime}c
=\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}c_jD[t_j]
=D[s].
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
For the third equality, \(G^{\dagger}G\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(G)\), and (5) places \(g\) in this range.

If \(\widetilde\zeta\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\) is another representer, apply the representer identity for both \(\widetilde\zeta\) and \(\zeta\) with \(s=\widetilde\zeta-\zeta\).  Subtraction gives
\[
E_P[(\widetilde\zeta-\zeta)^2]=0.
\tag{7}
\]
Hence the representer is unique as an element of \(L_2(P)\), including when \(G\) is singular.  Finally, (5) and \(G^{\dagger}GG^{\dagger}=G^{\dagger}\) imply
\[
E_P[\zeta^2]
=a^{\prime}Ga
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}GG^{\dagger}g
=g^{\prime}G^{\dagger}g.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (1)--(8) prove all population assertions.  They do not control estimated derivatives, Gram matrices, or Riesz representers, so they imply neither asymptotic linearity nor Wald validity for the growing-sieve construction.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(z_0\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(B_1(z),\ldots,B_L(z)\) be finitely many continuously differentiable real symmetric matrix maps on a neighborhood of \(z_0\), and suppose every nonzero eigenvalue of every \(B_j(z_0)\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa_0>0\).  If \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), then hard thresholding the eigenvalues of every \(B_j(\widehat z)\) at \(\tau_n\) recovers \(\operatorname{rank}B_j(z_0)\) simultaneously with probability tending to one.  On that event each thresholded inverse agrees with a continuously differentiable selected-rank inverse branch in a neighborhood of \(z_0\).  Consequently, any scalar map \(F\) obtained through finitely many additions, multiplications, divisions by quantities nonzero at \(z_0\), and these selected-rank inverses has, for \(d_0=DF(z_0)\),
\[
F_{\tau_n}(\widehat z)-F(z_0)
=d_0^{\prime}(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For a symmetric matrix coordinate \(B\), the derivative of its selected-rank inverse at \(B_0\), in direction \(H\), is the computable linear map
\[
D B_0^{\sharp}[H]
=-B_0^{\dagger}HB_0^{\dagger}
+(B_0^{\dagger})^2H(I-B_0B_0^{\dagger})
+(I-B_0^{\dagger}B_0)H(B_0^{\dagger})^2.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
It is enough to treat one matrix, because the collection is finite.  Write \(B_0=B(z_0)\).  Continuous differentiability implies local Lipschitz continuity, so
\[
\|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\tau_n).
\tag{9}
\]
For symmetric matrices the min--max characterization of ordered eigenvalues and
\(
|v^{\prime}\{B(\widehat z)-B_0\}v|
\leq\|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\)
for \(\|v\|=1\) give
\[
\max_k|\lambda_k\{B(\widehat z)\}-\lambda_k(B_0)|
\leq\|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{10}
\]
On an event whose probability tends to one, (9)--(10), \(\tau_n<\kappa_0/2\), and \(\|B(\widehat z)-B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\tau_n\) imply that every population zero eigenvalue has empirical absolute value below \(\tau_n\), whereas every population nonzero eigenvalue has empirical absolute value above \(\kappa_0/2>\tau_n\).  This proves rank recovery.

For completeness, the differentiable branch can be constructed without choosing eigenvectors.  Choose a positively oriented contour \(\gamma\) enclosing zero but no nonzero eigenvalue of \(B_0\).  For \(z\) sufficiently close to \(z_0\), set
\[
P_0(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\gamma}(wI-B(z))^{-1}\,dw.
\tag{11}
\]
The resolvent identity
\[
(wI-B_1)^{-1}-(wI-B_2)^{-1}
=(wI-B_1)^{-1}(B_1-B_2)(wI-B_2)^{-1}
\tag{12}
\]
shows directly, uniformly on the compact contour, that \(P_0(z)\) is continuously differentiable.  It is the spectral projector onto the eigenvalue cluster emanating from the null space of \(B_0\).  Define
\[
B^{\sharp}(z)
=(I-P_0(z))\{B(z)+P_0(z)\}^{-1}(I-P_0(z)).
\tag{13}
\]
The matrix inside braces is invertible near \(z_0\): on the range of \(P_0(z)\) its eigenvalues are the small eigenvalues of \(B(z)\) plus one, and on the complementary range they are separated from zero.  The inverse identity (12) and (11) therefore make (13) continuously differentiable.  At \(z_0\), (13) is \(B_0^{\dagger}\); on the rank-recovery event it is exactly the inverse that retains eigenvalues above \(\tau_n\) and sets the others to zero.

Differentiate the four Moore--Penrose equations at \(B_0\), or equivalently differentiate (11)--(13).  Multiplication by the range projector \(B_0B_0^{\dagger}=B_0^{\dagger}B_0\) on its four range/null blocks gives
\[
D B_0^{\sharp}[H]
=-B_0^{\dagger}HB_0^{\dagger}
+(B_0^{\dagger})^2H(I-B_0B_0^{\dagger})
+(I-B_0^{\dagger}B_0)H(B_0^{\dagger})^2,
\tag{14}
\]
including arbitrary null--null perturbations, whose derivative is zero.  Ordinary division is continuously differentiable wherever its denominator is nonzero.  The chain rule thus makes every stated finite composition \(F\) continuously differentiable near \(z_0\).  Its defining first-order expansion, together with \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), gives
\[
F^{\sharp}(\widehat z)-F(z_0)
=DF(z_0)(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{15}
\]
The thresholded and selected-rank maps agree with probability tending to one by (9)--(10), which proves the claim simultaneously for the finite collection.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P\) be a fixed interior law covered by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), where the deterministic complete-normal incidence basis uses every period-admissible OVS clean cohort \(\mathcal C_u=\{c\in\mathcal G:c>u\}\) for every restricted post-period \(u\).  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\), every support mass is positive, retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition hold, and \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are i.i.d.  Fix \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\), and impose the stated local-rank and positive-spectrum conditions on its finite KKT system.

Let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}\) be the finite set of cohort--eligibility cells appearing in a target score or in a complete OVS normal.  Define the observable finite vector \(U(O)\) by the coordinates
\[
U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}=\mathbf 1\{X=x_d,G=a,S=s\},
\quad
U^{(1)}_{d,a,s,u}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u,
\quad
U^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v,
\]
for \(d=1,\ldots,D\), \((a,s)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}\), and \(u,v\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), and put \(\mu=E_P[U(O)]\).  From a generic moment vector \(z\), reconstruct
\[
P_z(X=x_d)=\sum_{a,s}z^{(0)}_{d,a,s},
\qquad
p_{a,s,z}(x_d)=\frac{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}}{P_z(X=x_d)},
\]
\[
m_{a,s,u,z}(x_d)=\frac{z^{(1)}_{d,a,s,u}}{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}},
\qquad
E_z[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid X=x_d,G=a,S=s]
=\frac{z^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v}}{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}}.
\tag{16}
\]
Use (16) and Definitions \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) to form \(\theta_z\), \(\Psi_z\), \(\Omega_z=E_z[\Psi_z\Psi_z^{\prime}]\), \(\psi_z^0\), \(K_z(x_d)\), and \(r_z(x_d)\); every expectation here is evaluated from the displayed first and second cross-moments.  Solve the relevant blockwise or joint comparator KKT system at \(\Omega_z\) for \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}_z\), and define the explicit finite-dimensional map
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(z)
=b_z^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Omega_zb_z^{\mathrm{cmp}}
-\left\{E_z[(\psi_z^0)^2]
-\sum_{d=1}^DP_z(X=x_d)r_z(x_d)^{\prime}K_z(x_d)^{\dagger}r_z(x_d)\right\}.
\tag{17}
\]
Then \(F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mu)=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\).

Set \(\widehat\mu=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU(O_i)\), take \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\), replace every scalar probability denominator in (16) and in the subsequent score and normal reconstruction, including every target share \(\pi_{g,1}\), by its maximum with \(\tau_n\), and replace every Moore--Penrose inverse of a complete-normal matrix or comparator KKT matrix by the inverse retaining exactly the eigenvalues whose absolute values exceed \(\tau_n\).  Denote the resulting everywhere-defined map by \(F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}\) and set
\[
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}
=F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}(\widehat\mu).
\tag{18}
\]
Let \(F^{\circ}_{\widehat{\mathfrak r}}\) be the differentiable branch of (17) that retains the ranks selected in (18), calculate
\[
\widehat d= D F^{\circ}_{\widehat{\mathfrak r}}(\widehat\mu),
\qquad
\widehat\zeta_i=\widehat d^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\},
\qquad
\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\zeta_i^2,
\tag{19}
\]
where every inverse derivative is evaluated by the formula in Lemma \(\ref{lem:separated-spectral-delta}\).  Thus (18)--(19) are computable from empirical cell counts, first moments, and second cross-moments only.

Write \(d_P=DF^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\mu)\) and \(\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P}(O)=d_P^{\prime}\{U(O)-\mu\}\).  If
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\geq\delta_0>0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
0<V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
:=E_P[(\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P})^2]<\infty,
\tag{20}
\]
then
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P}(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}),
\tag{21}
\]
\[
\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
\longrightarrow_P V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}},
\qquad
\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}}
{\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}}}
\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{22}
\]
The corresponding two-sided Wald interval has pointwise limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\), and its lower endpoint is positive with probability tending to one.  This conclusion is pointwise at the fixed support and fixed ranks; it makes no continuous-covariate, growing-support, or rank-uniform claim.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first prove that (17) is the desired observed-law functional.  Because \(T\), the retained cell set, and the support of \(X\) are finite, each coordinate of a pairwise score or complete normal is, conditional on \((X,G,S)\), an affine function of \((\Delta Y_2,\ldots,\Delta Y_T)\).  Its conditional mean therefore depends only on the coordinates \(U^{(0)}\) and \(U^{(1)}\), and every conditional product of two such coordinates depends only on \(U^{(0)}\), \(U^{(1)}\), and \(U^{(2)}\).  The first two lines of (16) hence reconstruct \(p\), \(m\), \(q\), \(\pi\), and \(\theta\); the last line reconstructs every shared-cell cross-period covariance.  It follows directly from Definitions \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) that \(\Omega\), \(E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]\), \(K_P(x_d)\), and \(r_P(x_d)\) are exactly their values reconstructed from \(\mu\).  In particular, no independence between score coordinates sharing an outcome cell has been imposed.

Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), applied to the deterministic basis of all period-admissible OVS rows in the premise, gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{can}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-\sum_{d=1}^DP(X=x_d)r_P(x_d)^{\prime}K_P(x_d)^{\dagger}r_P(x_d).
\tag{23}
\]
The observable equalities give \(E_P[\Psi_P]=0\).  Hence the variance of the fixed comparator score is
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}
=b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{cmp}}.
\tag{24}
\]
The comparator definitions identify \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) with the loading coordinate of the corresponding Moore--Penrose KKT solution.  Subtracting (23) from (24) proves
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mu)
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{can}}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P).
\tag{25}
\]
Thus the causal efficiency target, the observed-law gap functional, and its estimator remain distinct: (25) identifies the second, while (18) estimates it.

Retained-cell overlap and the positive support masses imply
\[
\min_{d,(a,s)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}}
E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]>0.
\tag{26}
\]
The fourth-moment assumption gives
\(
|\Delta Y_u|^4\leq8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4)
\leq16\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|^4
\), so Cauchy--Schwarz gives, for all \(u,v\),
\[
E_P[(U^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v})^2]
\leq E_P[|\Delta Y_u|^2|\Delta Y_v|^2]
\leq\{E_P[|\Delta Y_u|^4]E_P[|\Delta Y_v|^4]\}^{1/2}<\infty.
\tag{27}
\]
All coordinates of \(U\) consequently have finite variance.  Since its dimension is fixed, Chebyshev's inequality coordinate by coordinate yields
\[
\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{28}
\]

On the neighborhood supplied by (26), the scalar ratios in (16), and hence every reconstructed first or second moment, are continuously differentiable functions of \(z\).  The relevant matrices are finite continuously differentiable matrix functions of \(z\).  At the fixed law, take the minimum over the nonzero absolute eigenvalues of all finitely many \(K_P(x_d)\) and comparator KKT matrices; the minimum is strictly positive, with the zero-rank matrices omitted.  The stipulated comparator spectrum supplies the same conclusion for its KKT matrices.  Since \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n=n^{-1/2+a}\to0\), Lemma \(\ref{lem:separated-spectral-delta}\), (26), and (28) show that, with probability tending to one, scalar clipping is inactive and every matrix rank is recovered.  On that event
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)
=F^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\widehat\mu),
\qquad
\widehat d=DF^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\widehat\mu).
\tag{29}
\]
The local-rank premise identifies this selected branch with the ordinary comparator functional along regular model submodels.  Formula (14) makes all generalized-inverse derivatives explicit, so the derivative in (19) is computable rather than existential.

Continuous differentiability and (28)--(29) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)
&=d_P^{\prime}(\widehat\mu-\mu)+o_P(n^{-1/2})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
d_P^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\mu\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
The summands in the last line are i.i.d. and mean zero.  Their variance is finite by (27) and is positive by (20).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\), applied to these scalar summands, proves (21).

It remains to verify studentization.  Equation (29) and continuity of the derivative imply \(\widehat d\to_Pd_P\).  Moreover, the weak law following from (27) gives
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|U(O_i)-\mu\|^2=O_P(1),
\qquad \|\widehat\mu-\mu\|=o_P(1).
\tag{31}
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, (31), and \(\widehat d-d_P=o_P(1)\),
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
\widehat d^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}
-d_P^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\mu\}
\right]^2=o_P(1).
\tag{32}
\]
The weak law for the squared fixed influence value, followed by (32), proves the variance consistency in (22).  To obtain the studentized limit without an additional theorem, fix \(\epsilon>0\).  On the event
\(
|\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/
V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}-1|\leq\epsilon
\), whose probability tends to one, the studentized statistic is bounded between deterministic \((1\pm\epsilon)^{-1/2}\) rescalings of the statistic in (21).  Letting \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), continuity of the standard normal distribution function proves the second assertion of (22) and the stated two-sided Wald coverage.

Finally, (20), (21), and variance consistency imply
\[
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}
-z_{1-\alpha/2}
\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)+o_P(1)
\geq\delta_0+o_P(1).
\tag{33}
\]
Therefore the lower endpoint is positive with probability tending to one.  The argument used neither nuisance-rate assumptions nor a growing dictionary; its finite-support and fixed-law spectral separation are exactly the announced scope.
